title: 2026-11-15 — Check a Python script's syntax with `ast.parse`, never `py_compile`, inside a run or work dir

data.head: ## 2026-11-15 — Check a Python script's syntax with `ast.parse`, never `py_compile`, inside a run or work dir

body:
`python3 -m py_compile` writes a `__pycache__/` beside the script it checks. Inside a chunk's work dir or a run dir,
the run-dir hygiene read refuses that bytecode, and a recursive `rm` to clear it is denied by the permission layer.
`python3 -c "import ast,sys; ast.parse(open(sys.argv[1]).read())" {script}` checks the same syntax and writes nothing.

On 2.1.287 the folder-trust dialog opens with its selection pointer `❯` one row above `Yes, I trust this folder`, so a
single Enter declines; one down arrow, then Enter on a re-read screen showing the pointer on the trust row, accepts it,
and the CLI then writes the folder's trust entry in `~/.claude.json` itself. A rig that types these keys reads its own
pty's screen before each key (security-plan §Data Protection holds the rule, the rig place and the residual).
Extended 2026-11-15: on 2.1.325 the options are unnumbered and the pointer opens on the non-trust row, and a cwd whose
`projects["<abs cwd>"].hasTrustDialogAccepted` reads `true` in `~/.claude.json` raises no trust dialog at all, so a
start there takes no key before the input box.

- 2026-11-15: A script that names a path under `target/e2e-home` keeps it as spelled and never resolves it: the link points outside the root to the per-user tmpfs, so a resolved path breaks every root-relative spelling the script makes and writes a host path into its records.

A live round on claude 2.1.325 read the dialog hold at its 3600 s ceiling: the wrapper expired the dialog after 3600013 ms with the hook still waiting and no human key during the hold.
On the founder's word the hold stands at 3600 s; its provisional mark (measured live only to about 660 s) is gone, and the ceiling now rests on one reading on one CLI version.
The only product change is the text of the hold ceiling's doc comment; no value, IPC method, event kind, flag, config key or CLI output changed.
The round also measured that the real CLI erases its input box on DEL, that 2.1.325 shows a folder-trust dialog with unnumbered options before any hook in a fresh cwd, and that the question dialog stays on the screen after the wrapper's expiry.
Matrix v2-03 (a wrapped start's first wheel lines) was not verified and is to be un-claimed; the rigs that drove the round are evidence scripts outside the product.

The rule that viola-core emits no telemetry, which rules over the changed component: the change is a doc comment only and adds no line, field or span, so the rule stands.

The order of run start events in events.ndjson: on a start whose folder-trust keys pass through the wrapper, wheel human-input comes before session-start, and a later human key adds no wheel line. A row holding the start order as wheel start then session-start does not hold on such a start.

The event stream is never rotated: a reused instance name keeps the earlier start's lines at the head of its events.ndjson (cursors are byte offsets, never rewritten), so a reader of one start's first lines must read that start's own lines.

Control characters and paste: the real CLI erases the input box on DEL (measured). Rows naming DEL only as a refused paste or send character gain a live fact beside them.

Local run outputs never uploaded, and test homes kept: the live frames stay only under a gitignored local path and are never committed or uploaded, and only closed-word summaries land. The kept home and frames are the operator's to delete.

Capability ledger stamps and verify as the only stamps writer: verify stamped claude 2.1.325 with 21 of 21 relied rows passing, on a test home only; the live home's ledger is not stamped for 2.1.325. This bears on the rows on cli_version, the cli_verified run-log field and the never-logged ledger contents.
